checks.evidence: Headline rows preserve E2 localization/tradeoff, E3 actionability, oracle-depth, and boundary-field numbers.
All six oracle-backed tasks have an action card and explicit counterpoint.
Task cards are based on visible-policy action cards and R354 profile-spec patches.
Evaluation ledger and paper drafts mention the R365 headline/case-study selector.
All inputs are tracked artifacts or current paper/docs; the script does not fetch data or rerun the profiler.
The paper text keeps outputs as operation/operation-stack evidence rather than new profiler abstractions.

claim: E2/E3 paper-ready headline rows and case cards can be mechanically extracted from existing labeled-trace artifacts

headline_rows.counterpoint: Fixed-session still has lower first-positive work (0.0044); dataset-native has higher top-5 recall (0.8665) at high work.
headline_rows.headline: Operation-stack query-aware rankings localize positives while inspecting much less work than flat summaries.
headline_rows.paper_takeaway: Use the operation stack as the primary triage surface when the goal is budgeted localization rather than full-recall summarization.
headline_rows.primary_numbers: 6 tasks / 4 datasets / 34539 operations / 3699 positives; Work@5 0.0937 vs flat 1; R@30% 0.39 vs fixed-session 0.3559.

headline_rows.counterpoint: The fixed-session result is a fragmentation result, not work dominance: operation_stack:query_aware has lower work-to-50%-recall on only 1/6 tasks, lower top-5 work on only 2/6 tasks, and lower work-to-first-positive on only 2/6 tasks.
headline_rows.headline: Operation stacks reduce fixed-session fragmentation for ranked inspection.
headline_rows.paper_takeaway: Session/span-shaped drilldown should be a secondary view; making it primary fragments positives across too many groups.
headline_rows.primary_numbers: Median groups 157.5 vs fixed-session 285; top-5 recall wins vs fixed-session 5/6; 30% budget inspects fewer groups on 5/6 tasks.

headline_rows.counterpoint: session-level AgentRewardBench labels do not prove latent subtask boundaries; positive-run units are a cross-dataset proxy, not human intent annotations
headline_rows.headline: The same ranked groups remain useful when scored at dataset-provided oracle depths.
headline_rows.paper_takeaway: The profiler can be evaluated at operation, session, positive-run, and OSWorld human-group depths without changing the two-object model.
headline_rows.primary_numbers: 24/24 rows lower top-5 unit work than flat; 20/24 rows beat fixed-session unit recall; 22/24 rows use fewer groups to 50% positives.

headline_rows.counterpoint: These are visible-profile configuration actions, not an automatic patch selector or human-productivity result.
headline_rows.headline: Profiler output identifies concrete view, ranker, and profile-spec changes.
headline_rows.paper_takeaway: The profiler is actionable because it names which stack fields, mappings, ranker policy, or drilldown should change.
headline_rows.primary_numbers: 27/36 objective rows need non-default actions; 25/36 require view changes; R354 accepts 5/6 patches with median AP delta 0.0376 and top-5 lift delta 0.575.

headline_rows.counterpoint: Boundary-derived fields improve AP and reduce groups, but they increase top-5 operation work and first-positive work on this held-out subset.
headline_rows.headline: The OSWorld-Human rejection is repaired by boundary-derived operation fields, not by adding a new profiler object.
headline_rows.paper_takeaway: Boundary backends are field derivation mechanisms whose outputs fold through the same operation-stack path.
headline_rows.primary_numbers: AP 0.2583 vs semantic-width 0.2402; groups 74 vs 108; top-5 recall delta 0.1111.
